row.evidence: Slite's pricing page lists SCIM only under Enterprise (Contact Sales); Basic ($10) and Pro ($20 per user/month billed yearly) do not include SCIM provisioning.
row.notes: New row. Plans: Basic $10, Pro $20 per user/month billed yearly, Enterprise custom. OpenID Connect SSO (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin, Auth0, Keycloak, ADFS) starts at Pro; SCIM provisioning and audit log are Enterprise-only on the pricing table. Slite publishes no SCIM setup guide: its help centre documents only JIT provisioning on Google or OpenID sign-in, 'lazy' deprovisioning (members archived when the IdP denies access at token refresh, or after 30 days of inactivity) and OIDC group sync. Help articles still use older plan names (Standard, Premium, Knowledge Suite). The public REST API (all plans) can only read users and groups.

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: Public API included (read-only for users). Google SSO enforcement only; no OpenID SSO.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: SCIM provisioning, audit log and service accounts are Enterprise-only.

scim.notes: SCIM appears only as a line on the pricing page; no Slite help or developer page documents a SCIM endpoint, token, IdP setup or supported operations.

user_api.notes: Public API is ticked on every plan; it is a content API whose user and group endpoints are read-only (look up users to set doc owners).

auth.notes: Personal API key (optionally read-only) or Enterprise service-account key, sent in the x-slite-api-key header.

capabilities.notes: The API reference lists only GET endpoints for users and groups; no write operations on users or groups exist in the reference.

endpoints.purpose: Search users by email, name or username

audit_log_api.notes: Audit log is an Enterprise feature on the pricing table; no audit-log API endpoint is in the API reference.

okta.notes: No Okta OIN page found (okta.com/integrations/slite/ returns 404); Slite's Okta guide has admins create their own OIDC web app in Okta.

entra.notes: No Slite tutorial in Microsoft Learn's SaaS app tutorial index; Slite documents Azure AD sign-in via a custom OpenID Connect app.

google.notes: Google sign-in with enforced Google Workspace authentication; no Google Workspace provisioning app documented.

fallbacks.other_sync: OIDC group provisioning (IdP groups synced to Slite user groups at sign-in and token refresh); lazy JIT deprovisioning archives members the IdP no longer grants
fallbacks.notes: Archived users cannot use Slite until restored; shared docs stay in channels and private docs are emailed as a backup .zip. Removing a user frees a license. Member list can be exported as CSV (no CSV import of users documented).

open_questions: Slite does not document how its Enterprise SCIM works (endpoint, token, IdPs, operations, attributes, deprovisioning).
Whether SCIM requires OIDC SSO to be configured is not stated.
Whether Slite is listed in the Okta, Entra, OneLogin or JumpCloud catalogues with provisioning is not confirmed.
Whether removing or archiving a member immediately frees the seat mid-term (the FAQ says the lower count shows on the renewal invoice).
